decision: No field-drop-order defect in inspected current source or original descriptor-capability commit. No edits proposed.
declaration_lines: capability.rs:119-127 declares content, temporary, executable, then ownership. Original e449d0a590 declaration identical. Worker isolated worktree capability bytes also identical.
apparent_confusion: Constructor expression at capability.rs:226-231 lists ownership first. Rust named-field initializer ordering does not change declaration field destruction order.
actual_custody: Every directory operation borrows self backed by Arc<Directories>; active normal use cannot coincide with final Arc destruction. Returned PendingWrite/ReadHandle declare File before retained Arc, so file closes before final directory custody may release. Directories declares three OwnedFd before Arc<Ownership>, so final destruction closes child descriptors before dropping final role locks. No custom Drop or spawned work in capability.rs changes this.
bounded_counterfactual: If ownership had been declared first, final lock release could precede child directory descriptor close. With final Arc reached there is no remaining safe Rust operation, directory close is not a promised sync/durability action, and no Drop implementation runs new namespace mutations. That alone would not establish overlapping live I/O or corruption; it would violate a stronger all-descriptors-closed-before-unlock contract if claimed. Actual declaration already enforces the stronger ordering.
limits: Source-level destruction/custody audit only, not a new runtime test or syscall trace, and no durability/power-loss inference. Existing cooperative namespace assumptions remain.
review_actions: Read-only repository/Git/source inspection; reviewer files only. No compiler/build/test invocation or worktree edit.
